title: is mid journey fine for game art assets?
author: shoukachidev
selftext:
had chatgpt before with plus but it was quite expensive and i dont like openAI as a whole so i now stick to claude only.  
But i still need concept arts etc so i am searching for alternatives.

has anyone experience working with mid journey or other platforms specifically for game art?

comments.author: Extempes
comments.body: Would say No..... In my Experience it wasnt worth it... Chatgpt/Codex do the Same better and more specific...

comments.author: wiggle_room1337
comments.body: You would have to tailor your game's style to what it can do, but ultimately there are very few success stories.

comments.author: Relative_Maize_6411
comments.body: I made Claude write an image generator with local model from huggingface works great for concept art if you wish that, I extended mine for it to draw game UI, repaint 3D objects, create seamless textures, even make 2D animated sprites. Also did the same for sound and music and also for 3D models using Trellis 1 with mcp servers Claude can connect to.

replies.author: shoukachidev
replies.body: that sounds interesting, gonna look into that!

replies.author: slowtractor
replies.body: When you switch from textures to sprites or UI, are those separate models or scripts, or is it one generator with different prompts? I'm curious how you set that up

replies.author: Relative_Maize_6411
replies.body:
It is same generator with same model but different prompts :)

  
Looks like this 

https://i.redd.it/t8a97er4qt3i1.png

replies.author: slowtractor
replies.body: I had pictured separate pipelines for each output type, so I had that backwards

comments.author: PM_Me_Those_
comments.body: I've found simply asking Claude "what tools or open source LLMs could be used to potentially get a better result?" has actually been very successful. I've forced it to 'bake-off' between multiple tools and workflows and I am finding it is able to overcome some of the areas where it just gets 'stuck' sometimes.

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body: Try nanobanana/gemini, I like both gemini and GPT imagegen, nano banana is a beast, but I only used them for concept art, not for direct game assets

comments.author: MidSerpent
comments.body:
No, it’s probably the worst for it.

It’s great for exploring looks but it’s terrible for consistency.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body:
it can be, but you need to really know your way around midjourney using things like reference images and srefs to get visual consistency out of it

these days, chatgpt, seedance, and seedream are sometimes better choices

midjourney is a great place to get that first image to get the style though

replies.author: katatonicmango
replies.body: I agree with this! I’m combining srefs in Midjourney to nail down a style and then giving those images to Claude.

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body: I have not been able to get anything usable out of it. It has been way too "creative". It is possibly the best at skin textures, but then comes the question how to get it from MidJourney to fit an UV map.
